questions: Psalm 42 shows someone being honest with God about feeling deeply down while still putting hope in Him. Why do you think both honesty and hope matter?
If a friend felt really down for a long time, what do you think would help them most?
prayForStudents: Pray students facing heavy days know they are not alone and can bring despair to God with hope.

guide.summary: This week's message, Depression, continued The Gospel (Mental Health) series. Students saw in Psalm 42 a writer who names deep sadness, even frustration with God, and still chooses to trust Him. The big idea was that we can trust God while experiencing depression and ask Him to turn despair into hope. They also heard that God cares, Christian community can walk with us, and wise help from counselors and other professionals is a gift when sadness lasts a long time or makes daily life hard.
guide.keyVerse: "Why, my soul, are you so dejected? Why are you in such turmoil? Put your hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God." Psalm 42:11 (CSB)
talkAboutIt: Psalm 42 shows someone being honest with God about feeling deeply down while still putting hope in Him. Why do you think both honesty and hope matter?
If a friend felt really down for a long time, what do you think would help them most?
What helps you feel less alone when life feels heavy, and how can our family be a safe place for that kind of honesty?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Read Psalm 42:6-11 together in a calm moment. Invite each person (only if they want) to finish one sentence: "Right now I feel..." and "I want to put my hope in God by..." Then name one trusted person outside the immediate moment (a parent, leader, counselor, or doctor) who can walk with your family if sadness feels heavy or lasting.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that You see us in dark and heavy places. Help our family be honest with You and with each other. Teach us to put our hope in You, and give us courage to ask for help when we need it. Amen.

questions: Romans 8 says nothing can separate us from the love of God in Christ. Which part of that promise feels most hopeful to you right now?
Who in your life helps you feel loved and safe to trust, and what do they do that makes the difference?
prayForStudents: Pray students know they are securely loved by God in Christ, and find trustworthy relationships at home and in Christian community.

guide.summary: This week's message, Attachment, continues The Gospel (Mental Health) series. Students hear that we learn love and trust through our closest relationships, starting with family, and that every one of us feels the strain when those relationships are hurt. Romans 8 shows that God is for us, gave His Son for us, and that nothing, including hardship or mental health struggles, can separate us from His love in Christ. That secure love, based on what God has done and not on our behavior, becomes the base for healthy relationships with others. Students also hear that when love and trust have been deeply broken, talking with a professional can be part of healing.
guide.keyVerse: "For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord." Romans 8:38-39 (CSB)
talkAboutIt: Romans 8 says nothing can separate us from the love of God in Christ. Which part of that promise feels most hopeful to you right now?
Who in your life helps you feel loved and safe to trust, and what do they do that makes the difference?
When have you felt unsure if you were loved or could trust someone? How does knowing God never changes help in moments like that?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Pick one regular moment this week, like a car ride or bedtime, and make it a no-pressure connection time. Read Romans 8:38-39 out loud together once, then let each person share one high and one low from the day while everyone else just listens. No fixing, no lectures. If someone shares something hard, thank them for trusting you with it, and if past hurts feel heavy, reach out to a pastor or counselor together.
guide.prayer: God, thank You that You are for us and that nothing can separate us from Your love in Christ Jesus. Help our family feel secure in Your love, be people others can trust, and be patient and gentle with each other. Heal any places where love and trust have been hurt. Amen.

title: No Midweek This Wednesday
message: There is no student Midweek on Wednesday, Nov 25, for Thanksgiving week. Enjoy the time together as a family! We'll be back on Wednesday, Dec 2, with "The Hype vs. The Hope" (Luke 2:8-14).

questions: What part of Christmas makes you feel the most stressed or pressured, and what part brings you the most real joy?
God chose ordinary, overlooked shepherds to hear the good news first. What does that tell you about how God sees you, even when you feel left out of the "perfect" Christmas picture?
tryThisAtHome: Before the holiday rush picks up, pick one night this week to slow down as a family. Read Luke 2:8-14 out loud together, then have each person name one Christmas pressure they would like to let go of this year and one simple thing that actually brings them joy. Choose one of those simple joys to do together this month, and give each other grace if the season doesn't look picture-perfect.

guide.summary: Christmas can feel heavy with pressure: perfect gifts, picture-perfect moments, and expectations that leave us exhausted. This week students looked at Luke 2:8-14, where God announced the birth of Jesus first to shepherds, ordinary people who were often overlooked. The angel told them not to be afraid and brought good news of great joy for all the people: a Savior has been born. The big idea: we often get caught up in the hype of Christmas, but its true meaning offers lasting hope. Jesus came for everyone, God sees the ones who feel unseen, and that is a reason to celebrate.
guide.keyVerse: But the angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for look, I proclaim to you good news of great joy that will be for all the people: Today in the city of David a Savior was born for you, who is the Messiah, the Lord.” Luke 2:10-11 (CSB)
talkAboutIt: What part of Christmas makes you feel the most stressed or pressured, and what part brings you the most real joy?
God chose ordinary, overlooked shepherds to hear the good news first. What does that tell you about how God sees you, even when you feel left out of the "perfect" Christmas picture?
The angel said, "Don't be afraid." Where could our family use that reminder right now, and what would it look like to trust that God is with us?
guide.tryThisAtHome: Before the holiday rush picks up, pick one night this week to slow down as a family. Read Luke 2:8-14 out loud together, then have each person name one Christmas pressure they would like to let go of this year and one simple thing that actually brings them joy. Choose one of those simple joys to do together this month, and give each other grace if the season doesn't look picture-perfect.
guide.prayer: God, thank You for sending Jesus, our Savior, as good news of great joy for all people. When this season gets loud and busy, help our family slow down and remember the hope we have in Him. Thank You that You see every one of us. Give us peace, take away our fear, and fill our home with real joy. Amen.
